details.readme:
Claude Code Game Studios

Turn a single Claude Code session into a full game development studio.
49 agents. 74 skills. One coordinated AI team.

--- ## Why This Exists Building a game solo with AI is powerful — but a single chat session has no structure. No one stops you from hardcoding magic numbers, skipping design docs, or writing spaghetti code. There's no QA pass, no design review, no one asking "does this actually fit the game's vision?" **Claude Code Game Studios** solves this by giving your AI session the structure of a real studio. Instead of one general-purpose assistant, you get 49 specialized agents organized into a studio hierarchy — directors who guard the vision, department leads who own their domains, and specialists who do the hands-on work. Each agent has defined responsibilities, escalation paths, and quality gates. The result: you still make every decision, but now you have a team that asks the right questions, catches mistakes early, and keeps your project organized from first brainstorm to launch. --- ## Table of Contents - [What's Included](#whats-included) - [Studio Hierarchy](#studio-hierarchy) - [Slash Commands](#slash-commands) - [Does it produce games, or documents?](#does-it-produce-games-or-documents) - [Getting Started](#getting-started) - [Configuration](#configuration) - [Upgrading](#upgrading) - [Project Structure](#project-structure) - [How It Works](#how-it-works) - [Design Philosophy](#design-philosophy) - [Customization](#customization) - [Platform Support](#platform-support) - [Community](#community) - [Supporting This Project](#supporting-this-project) - [License](#license) --- ## What's Included | Category | Count | Description | |----------|-------|-------------| | **Agents** | 49 | Specialized subagents across design, programming, art, audio, narrative, QA, and production | | **Skills** | 74 | Slash commands for every workflow phase (`/start`, `/design-system`, `/create-epics`, `/create-stories`, `/dev-story`, `/story-done`, etc.) | | **Hooks** | 15 | Automated validation on commits, pushes, asset changes, design-doc reads, writes and registries, session lifecycle, agent audit trail, and gap detection | | **Rules** | 14 | Path-scoped coding standards enforced when editing gameplay, engine, AI, UI, network code, scene and asset files, and more | | **Templates** | 62 | Document templates for GDDs, UX specs, ADRs, sprint plans, HUD design, accessibility, and more | ## Studio Hierarchy Agents are organized into three tiers, matching how real studios operate: ``` Tier 1 — Directors creative-director technical-director producer Tier 2 — Department Leads game-designer lead-programmer art-director audio-director narrative-director qa-lead release-manager localization-lead Tier 3 — Specialists gameplay-programmer engine-programmer ai-programmer network-programmer tools-programmer ui-programmer systems-designer level-designer economy-designer technical-artist sound-designer writer world-builder ux-designer prototyper performance-analyst devops-engineer analytics-engineer security-engineer qa-tester accessibility-specialist live-ops-designer community-manager ``` Each agent declares a model in its frontmatter: the three directors ask for Opus, `lead-programmer` and fifteen specialists name Sonnet, and the remaining thirty **inherit your session's model**. Treat the tiers as seniority of role, not as a billing plan — most of the studio runs on whatever model you are already using. ### Engine Specialists The template includes agent sets for all three major engines. Use the set that matches your project: | Engine | Lead Agent | Sub-Specialists | |--------|-----------|-----------------| | **Godot 4** | `godot-specialist` | GDScript, Shaders, GDExtension | | **Unity** | `unity-specialist` | DOTS/ECS, Shaders/VFX, Addressables, UI Toolkit | | **Unreal Engine 5** | `unreal-specialist` | GAS, Blueprints, Replication, UMG/CommonUI | ## Slash Commands Type `/` in Claude Code to access all 74 skills: **Onboarding & Navigation** `/start` `/help` `/project-stage-detect` `/setup-engine` `/adopt` `/settings` **Game Design** `/brainstorm` `/map-systems` `/design-system` `/quick-design` `/review-all-gdds` `/propagate-design-change` **Art & Assets** `/art-bible` `/asset-spec` `/asset-audit` **UX & Interface Design** `/ux-design` `/ux-review` **Architecture** `/create-architecture` `/architecture-decision` `/architecture-review` `/create-control-manifest` **Stories & Sprints** `/create-epics` `/create-stories` `/dev-story` `/sprint-plan` `/sprint-status` `/story-readiness` `/story-done` `/estimate` **Reviews & Analysis** `/design-review` `/code-review` `/balance-check` `/content-audit` `/scope-check` `/perf-profile` `/tech-debt` `/gate-check` `/consistency-check` `/security-audit` **QA & Testing** `/qa-plan` `/smoke-check` `/soak-test` `/regression-suite` `/test-setup` `/test-helpers` `/test-evidence-review` `/test-flakiness` `/skill-test` `/skill-improve` **Production** `/milestone-review` `/retrospective` `/bug-report` `/bug-triage` `/reverse-document` `/playtest-report` **Release** `/release-checklist` `/launch-checklist` `/changelog` `/patch-notes` `/hotfix` `/day-one-patch` **Creative & Content** `/prototype` `/vertical-slice` `/onboard` `/localize` **Team Orchestration** (coordinate multiple agents on a single feature) `/team-combat` `/team-narrative` `/team-ui` `/team-release` `/team-polish` `/team-audio` `/team-level` `/team-live-ops` `/team-qa` ## Does it produce games, or documents? A fair question, and the answer is a measurement rather than a sample project. Four games were built from one brief at different `modes.rigor` levels and the documents each wrote **before its first line of game code** were counted: | `modes.rigor` | Docs before first line of game code | Time | |---|---:|---:| | `minimal` | **1** (the one-page brief) | 0 min | | `standard` | 30 | 58 min | All of them produced a running, tested game. Two blind reviewers and a human playtest then ranked the `standard` build **last** — the extra 29 documents bought traceability, not a better game. ### It runs the game and looks at it The measurement above is about cost. The other half is whether the thing works, and for a game that means someone has to *look* at it — a passing test says nothing about a menu drawn off-screen. So a story that changes anything the player sees is not closed until the game has been launched, observed, and a screenshot retained in `production/qa/evidence/`. A parse check is not a run. This holds at every rigor level, including `minimal`, where automated tests are waived but the look is not. The games themselves are deliberately **not** shipped here: this is a template you clone to start your own project, and somebody else's game in your repo is clutter, not evidence. ## Getting Started ### Prerequisites - [Git](https://git-scm.com/) - [Claude Code](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/setup) — the native installer is recommended (`npm install -g @anthropic-ai/claude-code` also works, on Node.js 22+) - [Python 3](https://www.python.org/) — reads `project.yaml` for every skill and hook; without it every setting silently falls back to its default - Bash — runs every hook; built into macOS and Linux, and on Windows it comes with [Git for Windows](https://git-scm.com/downloads/win) - **Recommended**: [jq](https://jqlang.github.io/jq/) (for hook validation) Hooks fail gracefully if optional tools are missing — you just lose validation — with one deliberate exception: a commit that stages data JSON is blocked when there is no Python to validate it. ### Setup 1. **Clone or use as template**: ```bash git clone https://github.com/Donchitos/Claude-Code-Game-Studios.git my-game cd my-game ``` 2. **Open Claude Code in the project's root folder** (the one holding `CLAUDE.md` and `project.yaml`) and start a session: ```bash claude ``` Starting it in a subfolder such as `src/` skips the project's hooks, deny rules and ask-first permission mode. 3. **Run `/start`** — the system asks where you are (no idea, vague concept, clear design, existing work) and guides you to the right workflow. No assumptions. Or jump directly to a specific skill if you already know what you need: - `/brainstorm` — explore game ideas from scratch - `/setup-engine godot 4.7` — configure your engine if you already know - `/project-stage-detect` — analyze an existing project ## Configuration `project.yaml` at the repo root is the single source of truth for how the studio behaves on your project — engine, naming conventions, and a `modes` block that controls how much process every skill enforces. `/start` writes it for you; you rarely need to hand-edit it. The one question that matters most is **`modes.rigor`** — `minimal`, `standard`, or `full`. It's a single front door over six separate knobs (`workflow` — which GDD sections are required, `docs.density`, `qa.level`, `story_granularity`, `review_mode` — how many director agents review your work, and `team.size`), so `/start` asks it once instead of six times: - **`minimal`** (default) — jam-game speed. No GDDs required, terse docs, minimal QA evidence, solo review. `/start` → `/setup-engine` → `/brainstorm` (a one-page brief) → `/create-stories` → `/dev-story` ↔ `/story-done`. - **`standard`** — 5 required GDD sections, balanced doc depth, standard QA evidence, lean review. - **`full`** — all 8 GDD sections, thorough docs, full QA evidence on every story type, full director review. `minimal` is the default because the heavier tier costs more to reach working code without producing a better result, and gives nothing back when someone new picks the project up. Raise it in one `/settings` call when your project grows — `/help` and `/gate-check` will suggest it when they see the signs. Two escape hatches keep one setting from being a blunt instrument. **`system_overrides`** holds a single system to a higher standard than the rest of the project — your combat system gets the full treatment while everything else stays light. **`testing.strict`** sets, per test type (logic, integration, visual, UI, config), whether missing evidence blocks a story or merely warns. Any of the six underlying knobs can still be set individually if you want a mix (e.g. `workflow: full` with `docs.density: terse` — comprehensive but compact). Two of them — `review_mode` (`full` / `lean` / `solo`) and `team.size` — are also **personal**: rigor sets the team-wide default, but you can override them per-developer in a gitignored `project.local.yaml` without touching the shared

details.readme:
# Impeccable The design vocabulary for your coding agent. Steer with `polish` and `bolder`, review with `critique` and `audit`, and catch AI slop before it ships. From your project root: ```bash npx impeccable install ``` Reload your coding tool, then run `/impeccable init` in your agent (`$impeccable init` on Codex). Works with Claude Code, Cursor, Codex CLI, GitHub Copilot, Devin, Replit Agent, Gemini CLI, Grok Build, OpenCode, Google Antigravity, Kiro, Trae, Rovo Dev, Qoder, Mistral Vibe, Pi, Hermes Agent, DeepSeek Harness, and Veto. Full docs live at [impeccable.style/docs](https://impeccable.style/docs). | Without Impeccable | With Impeccable | |---|---| | ![Villa Castagneto built without Impeccable: cream background, a thin serif headline with an italic accent, two pill buttons, and flat vector illustrations in rounded cards](https://github.com/pbakaus/impeccable/raw/main/docs/images/readme-without.webp) | ![Villa Castagneto built with Impeccable: a full-bleed engraved night scene of the villa on its cliff above the sea, a condensed cream and vermilion headline, and a month strip along the bottom](https://github.com/pbakaus/impeccable/raw/main/docs/images/readme-with.webp) | Same model (Fable 5.1), same brief: a fourteen-room family guesthouse on the Ligurian coast. Without Impeccable, it builds the tasteful default: cream page, thin serif, italic accent, pill buttons. With it, the page is built around one picture: the house at night, seen from the water. For a full project, see the [Neo Mirai case study](https://impeccable.style/cases/neo-mirai): a conference site taken from mockup to shipped page. ## Why Inter for everything. Purple-to-blue gradients. Cards nested in cards, gray text on colored backgrounds, a rounded-square icon tile above every heading. Ask an agent for a page with no other guidance and these show up again and again, across models and projects. - **Words for what you want.** "Make it pop" leaves your agent to guess. `/impeccable bolder the pricing cards` loads a playbook written for that one move and points it at one target. - **A reviewer.** `critique` scores the design against usability heuristics and ranks what to fix first. `audit` checks accessibility, performance, theming, and responsive behavior, with findings ranked P0 (blocking) to P3 (polish). - **A slop detector.** 62 deterministic rules flag the tells above, plus quality problems like cramped padding and skipped headings. No LLM, no API key. Impeccable is strongest on interfaces that already exist: point it at a page or a component and iterate. It builds new pages too; see [Build something new](https://impeccable.style/docs/new-work) for how to get the most out of that harder mode. To start, pick one component: ``` /impeccable critique the pricing cards ``` ## How it works Run `/impeccable init` once per project. It reads your code, asks only what it can't infer (who the product is for, what it needs to do, the constraints), and writes `PRODUCT.md`. Every later command reads it. Run `/impeccable document` to capture your existing visual system in `DESIGN.md`, so changes stay on-brand. [More on context files](https://impeccable.style/docs/context). Then name a command and a target: ``` /impeccable critique the onboarding flow /impeccable quieter the landing page /impeccable polish settings /impeccable harden checkout ``` Or just describe what you want: `/impeccable redo this hero section`. Narrow targets get better results; a single section reviewed closely beats a whole page at a glance. Pin a command you use often with `/impeccable pin audit` to get `/audit` as its own shortcut. ### 24 commands | | Commands | |---|---| | **Steer** | `bolder` amplifies safe designs · `quieter` tones down loud ones · `distill` removes what the page doesn't need · `colorize` brings color to a gray interface · `typeset` fixes fonts, hierarchy, and sizing · `layout` fixes spacing and rhythm · `animate` adds transitions and interaction feedback · `delight` adds personality · `overdrive` goes for shaders, spring physics, and scroll-driven effects | | **Review** | `critique` is a scored UX review · `audit` is a technical quality report | | **Finish** | `polish` is the final pass before shipping · `harden` covers errors, i18n, overflow, and edge cases · `clarify` rewrites unclear copy · `adapt` handles screen sizes and devices · `optimize` fixes loading and rendering performance · `onboard` designs first-run flows and empty states | | **Iterate live** | `live` lets you pick an element in the browser and cycle through variants · `generate` produces variants of a named element without manual picking | | **Plan and set up** | `shape` plans UX before code · `init` writes `PRODUCT.md` · `document` writes `DESIGN.md` · `extract` pulls repeated patterns into your design system | The 24th, `craft`, is a deprecated alias for a plain build request. Type `/impeccable` alone to see the list in your agent. Each command has its own page: [impeccable.style/docs](https://impeccable.style/docs). On Codex, open `/skills` or type `$impeccable` instead of the slash command. ### Live mode `/impeccable live` opens your running dev server with an overlay. Select an element, pick a direction, and Impeccable hot-swaps variants in place. Accept one and it is written back to your source. It works with Vite, Next, SvelteKit, Astro, Nuxt, and plain HTML. [Iterate in the browser](https://impeccable.style/tutorials/iterate-live). Live mode edits a local checkout only; don't inject it into a deployed site or weaken a production CSP to make it work. Applying copy edits runs your `package.json`'s optional `impeccable:manual-edit-validate` script with your permissions, so review it before using live mode in an unfamiliar repo. ## Three ways to run the detector **In your agent.** The design hook scans every UI file your agent edits and hands the findings back before the agent calls the work done. This is where most slop gets caught: without the hook, the detector only runs when someone remembers to run it. It's available on Claude Code, Cursor, Codex, GitHub Copilot, Grok Build, and Hermes Agent, and the installer sets it up. Say yes. [Automatic design checks](https://impeccable.style/docs/hooks). **In CI or your terminal.** The CLI needs no agent: ```bash npx impeccable detect src/ # scan a directory npx impeccable detect https://example.com # scan a rendered page (uses your installed Chrome or Edge) npx impeccable detect --json . # machine-readable output npx impeccable detect --github src/ # GitHub Actions annotations npx impeccable detect --list-rules # every rule with its id and description ``` Source files like JSX and TSX get the pattern rules only. Rules that need a rendered page, such as low contrast and tiny text, run when you scan a URL, so point the CLI at your dev server too: `npx impeccable detect http://localhost:5173`. Exit code `2` means findings, `1` means a target couldn't be scanned. To allow your brand font everywhere, run `npx impeccable ignores add-value overused-font Inter --reason "Brand font"`. To turn a rule off for one file, add a comment: ``. [Run a detector scan](https://impeccable.style/docs/detector) · [Configuration and ignores](https://impeccable.style/docs/config). **In your browser.** The [Chrome extension](https://chromewebstore.google.com/detail/impeccable/bdkgmiklpdmaojlpflclinlofgjfpabf) overlays the same findings on any live page, yours or anyone else's. [Review with a visual overlay](https://impeccable.style/tutorials/critique-with-overlay). ## Installation ```bash npx impeccable install ``` The installer detects your coding tools, asks whether to install for this project or globally, and offers the design hook where your tool supports one. Accept the hook. Reload your tool afterward. `npx impeccable update` refreshes an existing install. For scripts, pass `--providers=claude,codex,cursor` and `--scope=project|global`. Three tools need one more step before the hook runs. In Codex, open `/hooks` and approve the project hook (again after an update that changes it). In Grok Build, run `/hooks-trust` or launch with `--trust`. In Hermes Agent, the hook is a plugin: run `hermes plugins enable impeccable-design-hook` once. [Allow the hook in your harness](https://impeccable.style/docs/hooks#allow-the-hook-in-your-harness). Node is only needed for `npx`. The skill itself runs a self-contained engine binary that ships next to it or downloads once into `~/.impeccable/bin/`.
Claude Code, Copilot, and Grok plugins **Claude Code:** `/plugin marketplace add pbakaus/impeccable`, then open `/plugin` and install Impeccable. **GitHub Copilot in VS Code:** install [Impeccable from the Visual Studio Marketplace](https://marketplace.visualstudio.com/items?itemName=renaissance-geek.impeccable) or run `code --install-extension renaissance-geek.impeccable`. Needs VS Code 1.109.3+, Copilot Chat, and a trusted workspace. It installs the skill without the hook. [Details](docs/VSCODE-EXTENSION.md). **Grok Build:** `grok plugin install pbakaus/impeccable#plugin --trust` installs the skill, agents, and hook.
Git submodule (a pinned version for the whole team) ```bash git submodule add https://github.com/pbakaus/impeccable vendor/impeccable npx impeccable link --source=vendor/impeccable --providers=claude,cursor ``` Commit `.gitmodules`, the submodule, and the generated links. Teammates run `git submodule update --init --recursive`. To upgrade, run `git submodule update --remote vendor/impeccable`, rerun the `link` command, and commit. Linking installs skills, not hooks. Existing skill folders stay put unless you pass `--force`.
Manual copy, no Node required Download the ZIP for your tool from [impeccable.style](https://impeccable.style), or clone this repo: each tool's build is committed at the repo root. Copy `skills/impeccable` from the folder below into the same place in your project, or into the global folder. | Tool | Repo folder | Global skills folder | |---|---|---| | Claude Code | `.claude/` | `~/.claude/skills/` | | Cursor | `.cursor/` | | | Codex CLI, Replit Agent | `.agents/` | `~/.agents/skills/` | | Devin | `.devin/` | `${XDG_CONFIG_HOME:-$HOME/.config}/devin/skills/` | | GitHub Copilot | `.github/` | | | Gemini CLI | `.gemini/` | | | Google Antigravity | `.agent/` | `~/.gemini/config/skills/` | | OpenCode | `.opencode/` | | | Grok Build | `.grok/` | `~/.grok/skills/` | | Hermes Agent | `.hermes/` | `${HERMES_HOME:-$HOME/.hermes}/skills/` | | DeepSeek Harness | `.dsh/` | `${DSH_HOME:-$HOME/.dsh}/skills/` | | Pi | `.pi/` | | | Qoder | `.qoder/` | `~/.qoder/skills/` | | Rovo Dev | `.rovodev/` | `~/.rovodev/skills/` | | Mistral Vibe | `.vibe/` | `~/.vibe/skills/` | | Trae | `.trae/` | `~/.trae/skills/` | | Trae China | `.trae-cn/` | `~/.trae-cn/skills/` | For example: `mkdir -p your-project/.claude/skills && cp -r .claude/skills/impeccable your-project/.claude/skills/`. Notes: - A manual copy skips the design hook and subagents. Run `npx impeccable install` to get them; it writes each tool's hook pointing at the right skill path. - OpenCode also needs `.opencode/commands/impeccable.md` copied into your project's `.opencode/commands/` to provide `/impeccable`. - Hermes asks you to trust project-local skills once: run `hermes skills trust` from the project root. Global installs need no trust step. - Cursor and Gemini CLI may need Agent Skills enabled in settings. See the [Cursor](https://cursor.com/docs/context/skills) and [Gemini CLI](https://geminicli.com/docs/cli/skills/) skills docs. - Restart Trae after copying. - `impeccable install` and `update` manage a DeepSeek Harness global copy only when `DSH_HOME` is inside your home di

details.readme:
Write HTML. Render video. Built for agents.

Studio | Quickstart | Showcase | Playground | Catalog | Docs | Discord

HyperFrames is an open-source framework for turning HTML, CSS, media, and seekable animations into deterministic MP4 videos. Use it locally with the CLI, from AI coding agents with skills, or as the rendering core behind hosted authoring workflows. Using Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, or another coding agent? Run `npx hyperframes skills update` once, then ask your agent to make a video. ## Quick Start ### With an AI coding agent For Claude Code, install the versioned plugin: ```bash claude plugin marketplace add heygen-com/hyperframes claude plugin install hyperframes@hyperframes ``` To enable auto-update for the **hyperframes** marketplace, run `claude` in a terminal in your project. In Claude Code's terminal UI, run `/plugin`, then select **Marketplaces** → **hyperframes** → **Enable auto-update**. Afterward, use `/hyperframes:hyperframes`. See the [plugin guide](docs/guides/plugins.mdx) for Copilot, VS Code, Cursor, Gemini CLI, updates, and migration. For standalone skills (including OpenCode), use: ```bash npx skills add heygen-com/hyperframes ``` > The picker opens with nothing pre-selected — the **Core Skills** group is all you need; `/slideshow`, `/remotion-to-hyperframes` and `/figma` install on demand. Agents and non-interactive runs should use `npx hyperframes skills update` instead — it installs exactly the core set, whereas `skills add --all` installs all 7 published skills. The six repo-internal skills under `.claude/skills` / `.agents/skills` are excluded by default. For the full published set use `npx hyperframes skills`. > > `skills add` resolves the skills.sh registry blob, which can lag `main` by hours. `npx hyperframes skills update` installs from the current `main`, so reach for it when you need the newest copy of a skill. Run project-local installs from your video project's directory. From a HyperFrames checkout, use `npx hyperframes skills update` for a global install instead: a project-local installer target can overlap the tracked `skills/` source and overwrite uncommitted edits. See [contributor setup](CONTRIBUTING.md#getting-started). Try a prompt like: > Using `/hyperframes`, create a 10-second product intro with a fade-in title, a background video, and subtle background music. The skills teach agents the HyperFrames production loop: plan the video, write valid HTML, wire seekable animations, add media, lint, preview, and render. They work with Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, Gemini CLI, IBM Bob, and other coding agents that support skills. ## Skills HyperFrames ships 7 skills. Make any video by asking for it; the `/hyperframes` skill carries the contract and the references (film, captions, overlays, motion, look). Read it first. For standalone installation, default to the **core set** (`/hyperframes`, `/hyperframes-cli`, `/hyperframes-registry`, `/media-use`). `npx hyperframes skills update` installs exactly that from anywhere; the interactive picker (`npx skills add heygen-com/hyperframes`) lists it as the "Core Skills" group, nothing pre-selected. The picker is interactive-only — a non-interactive or agent run without `--skill` installs all 7. Use `npx skills add heygen-com/hyperframes --all` to install the complete published set deliberately (skips the picker), or `npx skills add heygen-com/hyperframes --skill ` for just one (bare name, no leading `/`). Standalone installs stay lean after that: `npx hyperframes init` installs the **core set** only when it is missing and never touches a skill you already have (`npx hyperframes skills update` refreshes them, and never removes one); `/figma`, `/slideshow` and `/remotion-to-hyperframes` install **on demand** with `npx hyperframes skills update `. Nothing re-pulls the full set behind your back. ### Plugin packages Plugins bundle the full skill catalog and use their agent's update manager. `bun run package:agent-plugin` builds the committed portable ZIP, source metadata, and SHA-256 checksum. See the [maintainer checklist](docs/contributing/agent-plugins.mdx). ### Upload to Codex Build the upload-ready Codex plugin archive from the committed `HEAD` version of the manifest, brand assets, and skills: ```bash bun run package:codex-plugin ``` This writes `dist/hyperframes-plugin.zip` with a `hyperframes/` root folder and fails if the archive exceeds Codex's 100 MB upload limit. ### Core set | Skill | Use when | | ----------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | | `/hyperframes` | **Read first** for any request to make, edit, animate or render a video, motion graphic, captions or overlays with HyperFrames (HTML rendered to video). details.readme:
Website · Download · Documentation · Release notes · Roadmap · Project status · Contributing

# Horizon Horizon is Minecraft: Java Edition 26.3 rewritten in Rust: a native game that reads the same worlds, follows the same rules and generates the same terrain as the Java game, and is checked against it by more than 300 differential harnesses. You play it through a small launcher, on the files from your own copy of Minecraft. It is free, open source and unofficial. > Not an official Minecraft product. Not approved by or associated with Mojang or Microsoft. Horizon contains no Minecraft code, assets or data: you need your own legally obtained copy of Minecraft: Java Edition 26.3. ## Download Horizon is installed through **the Horizon launcher**. Get it from [playhorizon.dev](https://playhorizon.dev) (the Download button picks your system) or from [the launcher releases](https://github.com/horizon-rust/horizon/releases?q=launcher-v&expanded=true), for Linux x86-64, macOS on Apple Silicon or Windows x64. The launcher installs the game and keeps it up to date with each new build (Horizon ships on one channel, the Nightly), prepares its files from your copy of Minecraft (your own install, or downloaded from Mojang for your account), and updates itself. **You need** a Microsoft account that owns Minecraft: Java Edition (the launcher signs in with it, as other launchers do; see [Microsoft account](docs/microsoft-account.md)) and a GPU with Vulkan or OpenGL 3.3 on Linux, Vulkan or DirectX 12 on Windows, or any Apple Silicon Mac. Nothing else: with no Minecraft on your computer, Play downloads 26.3 and the Java it needs from Mojang for your account, as the official launcher does, then prepares it once. An install you already have (the official launcher, Prism, MultiMC and other launchers all work) is used instead. Step by step, with macOS's first-open prompt and the first launch: [Install and first launch](https://playhorizon.dev/docs/install).
## What works today The [documentation](https://playhorizon.dev/docs/) covers each of these. - **The game:** singleplayer with vanilla's world generation, mobs, villagers, raids, redstone, every command, the HUD and the recipe book, on saves in vanilla's format. Worlds from 1.8 to 26.2 are upgraded as vanilla does. [Status table](#project-status). - **Horizon's own extras:** new menus (vanilla's are one setting away), graphics presets, distant terrain up to 1024 chunks, controller support, optional zoom, minimap and more, all off by default where they would change the vanilla look. See [Settings](https://playhorizon.dev/docs/settings). - **Resource packs and data packs:** resource packs work, and data packs load functions, predicates, item modifiers and world generation (vanilla's heights and biomes for now). - **Playing with others:** invite friends from the pause menu's Friends button with a code, Open to LAN, and joining servers, online-mode ones with the Microsoft account the launcher signs in with. See [Multiplayer](https://playhorizon.dev/docs/multiplayer). - **Mods:** content mods add blocks, items and data, and native mods change the game's own Rust code, built by the launcher on your copy, with no Rust to install. Horizon's own (Zoom, FPS Counter, Keystrokes, Minimap, Recipes and Coordinates HUD) are native mods. Java mod jars do not run in Horizon. See [Mods and data packs](https://playhorizon.dev/docs/mods). Screenshots, captured in the Rust client itself with vanilla assets and no mods or shaders:
## Host a server The launcher's **Servers** page creates, starts, backs up and updates a Horizon server with buttons, and invites friends over Tailscale. On a VPS, `horizon-server` installs with one command and runs without Java. Guide: [Host a server](https://playhorizon.dev/docs/hosting) ([reference](docs/hosting.md)). ## Modpacks The launcher's **Modpacks** page imports a Modrinth or CurseForge pack, shows which of its mods Horizon can carry over, and plays the ones it can as their own profile. Today that means content mods made of data and assets; mods with Java code are not ported yet. See [Modpacks](https://playhorizon.dev/docs/modpacks). ## Agent control AI agents and scripts can play Horizon. `horizon-ctl`, shipped beside the game in every release folder, is a command line that reads the game as JSON and acts like a player; `horizon-ctl mcp` serves the same commands as an MCP server (one tool per command, screenshots returned as images). ```sh horizon-ctl launch --world Survival --seed 5 --wait # finds the version the launcher installed horizon-ctl state # position, health, food, target, screen... horizon-ctl find-block birch_log # the nearest logs horizon-ctl goto -0.5 65 -2.5 --near 2.5 # walks there along a path horizon-ctl break -1 65 -3 # mines it; replies with the drops horizon-ctl open-inventory && horizon-ctl click-slot 0 # menus: slots, buttons by label, text fields ``` Commands block until the action is done and reply with what happened; errors are JSON with distinct exit codes, `horizon-ctl help` lists every command and `horizon-ctl COMMAND --help` explains one with examples. It talks to the game over a Unix socket on Linux and macOS and over a token-protected localhost port on Windows. See [Agent control in the native client guide](docs/native-client.md#agent-control-horizon-ctl-and-mcp). ## Build from source For developers. Requirements: Rust 1.90 or newer, Python 3.10 or newer, JDK 25, and on Linux the ALSA and udev development headers (`libasound2-dev libudev-dev` on Debian and Ubuntu). Development and the vanilla harnesses run on Linux. Horizon contains no game files, and `horizon-prepare` never downloads them (the launcher downloads them from Mojang only for a signed-in account that owns the game). It builds its resources from **your own copy** of Minecraft: Java Edition 26.3, verified against the checksums in `research-lock.json`: 1. **Client:** install Java Edition with the official launcher and play 26.3 once. Horizon reads `versions/26.3/`, `libraries/` and `assets/` from the launcher's game directory (`~/.minecraft` on Linux). If yours lives elsewhere, pass `--minecraft-dir` or set `HORIZON_MINECRAFT_DIR`. 2. **Server jar:** the 26.3 server jar, from the `downloads.server.url` in your launcher's `versions/26.3/26.3.json` (or [minecraft.net/download/server](https://www.minecraft.net/en-us/download/server) while 26.3 is the current release). Pass it with `--server-jar` or set `HORIZON_SERVER_JAR`. It is only needed the first time. ```sh git clone https://github.com/horizon-rust/horizon.git cd horizon cargo run --release -p horizon-prepare -- --prepare --server-jar ~/Downloads/server.jar # needs JDK 25 cargo run --release -p horizon-prepare -- sounds # optional: sounds from your launcher install cargo run --release -p horizon-client ``` Everything prepared lands in the gitignored `.local/`. It is derived from the game: never commit it or share it. The client starts on the title screen. Command-line options (`--world`, `--seed`, `--creative`, `--render-distance`, `--dedicated`), controls, scripting through `horizon-ctl` and the architecture are described in [the native client guide](docs/native-client.md). The rest of the developer documentation is indexed in [docs/README.md](docs/README.md), including [the parity workflow](docs/parity-workflow.md). ## Roadmap What is being done now, what comes next and where you can help, in plain words and in technical detail: [ROADMAP.md](ROADMAP.md). [playhorizon.dev/hub](https://playhorizon.dev/hub) shows it with the work board, the journal of what shipped and how to help. ## Contributing Issues and pull requests are welcome: see [CONTRIBUTING.md](CONTRIBUTING.md) for how we work (vanilla first, small pull requests, labels), or [the contributing guide](https://playhorizon.dev/docs/contributing) on the site. Questions and ideas: [Discord](https://discord.gg/HcTeMZxe5E). Before opening a pull request, run the self-check and paste the block it prints: ```sh git config core.hooksPath .githooks python3 tools/pr_ready.py ``` It runs rustfmt, clippy with warnings denied, the tests of the crates you touched, the Python tests, the public-tree check, and the vanilla harnesses your change can affect. CI runs the same checks on GitHub's Linux runners; the vanilla harnesses need the game, which Horizon never downloads, so they run on a maintainer's computer holding their own copy. Never commit game files, decompiled source or prepared resources: `tools/check_public_tree.py` rejects them, and tracked Java is allowed only under the project's own `dev/horizonlab` namespace. ## Project status **Player-visible gaps: 833 open** of the 833 the [port ledger](tools/port_ledger.py) found, reading every vanilla 26.3 method against Horizon's code: vanilla behaviour a player would notice that Horizon doesn't have yet. By area: Screens, HUD and client packets [197](https://github.com/horizon-rust/horizon/issues/3518); Entity and block rendering, models [129](https://github.com/horizon-rust/horizon/issues/3519); Animals [110](https://github.com/horizon-rust/horizon/issues/3512); Server and players on the server [106](https://github.com/horizon-rust/horizon/issues/3520); Blocks, redstone and fluids [86](https://github.com/horizon-rust/horizon/issues/3516); Entities, pro

details.readme:
# FunASR.NET

**用 .NET 10 和纯 C# 推理实现普通话识别、语音合成与电话音频处理。** 核心命名空间 `FunAsrNet`，支持 CPU SIMD 和显式启用的 Vulkan GPU 混合后端。

基于 [QwenAudio/Fun-ASR](https://github.com/QwenAudio/Fun-ASR) 固定版本架构的独立社区实现，**不是官方 .NET SDK，也不是整个 FunASR 工具箱的移植**。围绕固定 F16 编码器、Qwen3 Q8_0 解码器、FSMN VAD 与两种中文 VITS 模型验证，不承诺兼容上游所有模型及语言。

## 纯 .NET 的实现范围

- 默认 CPU 的模型读取、特征、神经网络算子、解码、VAD、中文前端和 TTS 均由 C# 实现，不是给原生引擎包一层接口。
- 核心、CLI 和 Web 服务不依赖 Python、ONNX Runtime、ggml、sherpa-onnx 或 RKNN 推理库。ONNX/GGUF 在这里是文件格式；自有 ONNX 解释器只支持固定模型需要的子集。
- 使用 .NET SIMD、ARM64 NEON/SDOT、池缓冲、共享只读权重和有界队列。ASR 默认布局按硬件选择，x64 用行主序 SIMD，ARM64 用 NEON/SDOT 交错内核；各平台优化程度不同。
- 可选 Vulkan 用 C# 调度系统原生 GPU 驱动，执行嵌入 SPIR-V。仓库保留 GLSL 源码字符串；“纯 .NET”描述默认 CPU 推理，不表示 GPU 无需原生驱动。
- `tools/FunAsrNet.NativeReference` 单独引用原生 ORT，只作开发对照，不在主解决方案中，不是产品依赖。

详见 [架构](doc/architecture.md) 和 [第三方说明](THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md)。

## 功能

| 功能 | 当前实现 |
|---|---|
| ASR | WAV 转写；固定 F16 编码器、Q8_0 解码器 |
| 实时转写 | WebSocket、VAD 切句、可修订预览；不是逐帧增量编码 |
| 中文 TTS | Huayan 1 位、AISHELL3 174 位发音人，安装两模型后共 175 位 |
| 浏览器 Demo | 麦克风实时转写、上传 WAV、TTS 播放/下载，发音人搜索列表 |
| 电话音频 | PCM16、G.711 PCMA/PCMU、重采样，可接自研 SIP/PJSIP 媒体层 |
| 并发 | 独立会话状态、只读权重共享、队列/配额/取消和缓冲所有权管理 |
| 可选 GPU | Vulkan FP32 矩阵/卷积、原 Q8_0 投影；剩余算子在 CPU |

TTS 可设置语速、音量、采样率、格式、发音人、种子和随机度；尚无独立音高/情绪控制。服务不实现 SIP 信令、RTP 抖动缓冲或 AEC。

## 构建与运行

安装 .NET 10 SDK（`global.json` 最低 10.0.300），在仓库根目录执行：

```shell
dotnet build FunAsrNet.sln -c Release
dotnet run --project tests/FunAsrNet.Checks -c Release --no-build
dotnet run --project tools/FunAsrNet.CodeStyle -c Release --no-build -- .
```

**权重不在仓库内。** 按 [模型清单](doc/models.md) 准备 `models/` 并校验 SHA-256。ASR/VAD 需要兼容 GGUF，暂未提供一键下载的公开 GGUF 镜像或转换工具。克隆代码可运行无模型数值检查，不能直接启动完整服务。

```shell
dotnet publish src/FunAsrNet.Server -c Release -o artifacts/server
dotnet artifacts/server/FunAsrNet.Server.dll --urls http://localhost:18080 --models models --lexicon assets/mandarin-lexicon.json --threads 4
```

打开 `http://localhost:18080` 使用三个 Demo。远程麦克风需 HTTPS，见 [部署](doc/deployment.md)。默认 Web 服务用 CPU；Vulkan 通过代码或基准工具显式选择，服务暂未提供 GPU 配置开关。

```shell
dotnet run --project src/FunAsrNet.Cli -c Release -- asr --enc models/funasr-encoder-f16.gguf --llm models/qwen3-0.6b-q8_0.gguf --wav input.wav --threads 4 --repeat 3
dotnet run --project src/FunAsrNet.Cli -c Release -- tts --model models/aishell3/model.onnx --lexicon models/aishell3/lexicon.txt --tokens models/aishell3/tokens.txt --speaker 50 --text "您好，欢迎致电。" --rate 8000 --out speech.wav
```

## C# 调用

引用 `src/FunAsrNet/FunAsrNet.csproj`，尚未发布 NuGet 包。同一推理实例须串行使用。

```csharp
using FunAsrNet;

var asr = new FunAsr("models/funasr-encoder-f16.gguf", "models/qwen3-0.6b-q8_0.gguf", threads: 4);
var (samples, rate) = AudioFile.ReadWave("input.wav");
var result = asr.Transcribe(AudioFile.Resample(samples, rate, 16000), maxTokens: 128);
Console.WriteLine(result.Text);

var tts = new MandarinTts("models/zh_CN-huayan-medium.onnx", "assets/mandarin-lexicon.json", threads: 4);
var speech = tts.Synthesize("您好，欢迎致电。", speed: 1, seed: 1);
AudioFile.WriteWave("speech.wav", speech, tts.NativeSampleRate);
```

GPU 另外引用 `src/FunAsrNet.Vulkan/FunAsrNet.Vulkan.csproj`，首次推理前设置：

```csharp
using FunAsrNet.Vulkan;

using var gpu = new VulkanFloatBackend();
var gpuAsr = new FunAsr("models/funasr-encoder-f16.gguf", "models/qwen3-0.6b-q8_0.gguf", threads: 4)
{
    FloatBackend = gpu
};
var gpuTts = new MandarinTts("models/zh_CN-huayan-medium.onnx", "assets/mandarin-lexicon.json", threads: 4)
{
    FloatBackend = gpu
};
// 所有推理须在 gpu 释放前完成；模型实例仍串行使用。
```

## 与原版的真实速度对比

### Windows：第七轮 GPU 优化与 CPU/GPU 完整对比（2026-10-12）

本机 i7-12700、RTX 3060、四线程、相同模型和输入，默认 CPU 推理保持纯 C#。本轮 GPU 将编码器两层投影连续执行，减少中间回传，并优化 FP32 累加器、Q8 整数点积与短栅栏等待。**ASR GPU 比上一版减少 14.8%～19.4% 耗时，TTS 减少 3.9%～8.0%；仍为同轮原版 GPU 的 3.14～5.50 倍耗时，尚未追平。**

预热后完整调用中位数，单位秒；ASR 原版为 C++ CPU / 原计算图 CUDA 编码器和解码器，TTS 原版为 ORT CPU / CUDA：

| 项目 | C# CPU | 原版 CPU | C# Vulkan | 原版 GPU |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| ASR 6.000 秒 PCMA | 0.720 | 0.773 | 0.349 | 0.111 |
| ASR 5.616 秒 PCMU | 0.845 | 0.880 | 0.407 | 0.116 |
| ASR 28.000 秒重复样例 | 2.881 | 3.039 | 1.344 | 0.263 |
| ASR 6.000 秒原始 PCM | 0.670 | 0.730 | 0.346 | 0.098 |
| ASR 官方 PCMA | 0.679 | 0.756 | 0.353 | 0.103 |
| TTS Huayan 0 号 | 0.141 | 0.108 | 0.154 | 0.028 |
| TTS AISHELL3 50 号 | 0.067 | 0.046 | 0.087 | 0.026 |

模型/后端初始化中位数，单位秒；ASR 取上表短 PCMA 的双模型初始化，两种 TTS 分别加载对应 ONNX：

| 模型 | C# CPU | 原版 CPU | C# Vulkan | 原版 GPU |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| ASR 编码器 + 解码器 | 0.800 | 0.322 | 1.108 | 0.782 |
| Huayan | 0.094 | 0.868 | 0.411 | 1.019 |
| AISHELL3 | 0.068 | 0.551 | 0.378 | 0.672 |

Vulkan 的首次权重上传另计入首次推理。短 ASR 的“初始化 + 首次推理”为 C# CPU **1.621 秒**、C++ CPU **1.158 秒**、C# Vulkan **3.478 秒**、原图 CUDA **1.033 秒**。文件/驱动缓存未清空，不含进程或服务启动。**本轮 GPU 初始化稍慢，两个 TTS 的初始化加首次推理也变慢；热态改善不等于启动改善。**

CPU 热态相对上一版约 -0.8%～+1.9%，没有新整体加速。当前 TTS 的 C# Vulkan 仍慢于 C# CPU。CPU/GPU 各 210 次正式调用、42 次首次调用，每个热态表格单元十个样本，初始化单元两个新进程样本。五份 ASR 在各自 CPU 或 GPU 对照中三方转写一致；新旧 GPU 的 53 个 ASR 张量快照及 TTS 波形逐位相同。

所有输入的加载、首次推理、P95、上一版对照、精度与原图 CUDA 适配边界见 [第七轮完整报告](doc/gpu-round7-20261012.md)，原始记录及散列均随报告保留。结果仅适用于本机这些输入，不代表语言优势、RK3588 性能或实时麦克风识别率。下方保留历史测量。

### Windows：历史第六轮模型加载与 GPU 优化（2026-10-12）

已移除当前版本的六个 Python 复测/汇总脚本，统一使用 [C# 对比入口](tools/FunAsrNet.Compare/README.md)；历史原始数据保留。默认 CPU 推理仍不依赖原生引擎。

两份 ASR GGUF 的读取与解包中位数从 **3.203 秒降到 0.723 秒，耗时减少 77.4%**；托管分配从 3.076 GB 降到 1.812 GB。12 个新进程样本，未清空文件缓存，不含推理或 GPU 首次上传。短 ASR 的 CPU 模型初始化与首次转写之和从 4.061 秒降到 1.606 秒，同轮原版为 1.168 秒；仍不能当作完整服务冷启动。

RTX 3060、相同模型/输入、四线程；每格十次预热后的正式样本：

| 项目 | 上一版 C# Vulkan | 本次 C# Vulkan | 同轮原版 GPU | 本轮耗时减少 |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| ASR 6.000 秒 PCMA | 0.495 秒 | 0.427 秒 | 0.107 秒 | 13.8% |
| ASR 5.616 秒 PCMU | 0.553 秒 | 0.480 秒 | 0.125 秒 | 13.2% |

### Windows：历史第五轮 ASR CPU 优化（2026-10-12）

同轮 TTS Huayan 为 0.138 / 0.103 秒、AISHELL3 为 0.065 / 0.044 秒（C# / ORT CPU），仍未追平。以下表格为各自版本的历史结果。

### Windows：历史第四轮纯 C# CPU（2026-10-12）

### RK3588：纯 CPU 原版对照快照（2026-10-12，`ab83e5b`）

repository.description: Play a finished motion-graphics ad in sync with the rough drafts it grew from, and export the breakdown as MP4.

details.readme:
Null Motion

See how a finished motion-graphics ad was built — draft by draft, frame by frame.
Final film on top. Rough HyperFrames drafts underneath. Export the breakdown as one MP4.

If this helps you study or pitch motion work, a ⭐ makes it easier for others to find.

Top: the finished ad. Bottom: one plain black-and-white HyperFrames draft per section. The playhead and the orange outline follow the film frame for frame.

## Quick start ```sh git clone https://github.com/blixvip/NullMotion.git && cd NullMotion npm start # Node 22+, nothing to install ``` Then open ****, pick a reference, and press **Download → Whole preview** (Chrome or Edge) to get the MP4. No `npm install`, no API keys, no account. Three references ship with the repo, so it works on the first run. > **Not the same as Null Studio.** This repo is the free, local launch-film preview. Pause cuts, captions, and YouTube, Twitch, and Kick clips are **Null Studio**, a separate hosted product at [nullmotion.com](https://www.nullmotion.com/). They are not in this code.

What it does · Showcase · How it works · Bring your own references · FAQ · Project layout · Contributing · Community

--- ## What it does Motion-graphics ads look effortless, but every one starts as a rough plan: which idea goes in which section, and when each move lands. Null Motion puts that plan and the finished film side by side, so you can study how a great ad is built, pitch a concept, or export the whole breakdown as one video. - **The final film on top.** The full ad, full width, playing on a loop. - **Its drafts underneath.** Each section (Hook, Reveal, App, End card…) has a plain HyperFrames scene: black and white, Arial type, flat shapes, one simple move. It shows the idea before the polish. - **Everything in sync.** A playhead runs across the drafts. The draft for the section on screen follows the film frame for frame and gets an orange outline. The others keep looping their own part. - **One-click export.** **Download → Whole preview** renders the film and its drafts frame by frame into a 1920-wide, 24 Mbps MP4 with the film's audio.

## Showcase The repo ships three references with their drafts, ready to play: | | Reference | Length | Drafts | |---|---|---|---| | | **Infinite · Global payments** | 0:30 | 7 | | | **SaaS · Launch sequence** | 1:02 | 8 | | | **Motion study 08** | 0:03 | 3 |

These clips come from other creators and are used as examples. They are not claims of commissioned work. ### 🎬 Show what you made Exported a breakdown or built drafts for your own ad? Post it in the **[Discord](https://discord.gg/zEB4VjmfSb)**. We'd love to see it. ## How it works 1. **Sections.** `scripts/plan-sections.mjs` splits each reference into 3–8 sections at real scene changes (FFmpeg scene detection) and keeps every cut. Two-beat drafts switch at the exact moment the film cuts. 2. **Drafts.** `public/drafts.mjs` is a small HyperFrames engine: each draft is a 640×360 HTML scene on a paused GSAP timeline. A section is described by one or two *beats* (`text`, `logo`, `phone`, `window`, `input`, `chat`, `cards`, `list`, `chart`, `cloud`…), written to match the real frame's layout, text and timing. 3. **Playback.** The page drives every draft's timeline from the film's clock. The active section follows the film, and the others loop. 4. **Export.** A hidden copy of the film plays at half speed. `requestVideoFrameCallback` captures every decoded frame, the drafts are drawn at that frame's exact time, and WebCodecs encodes it at 24 Mbps with the frame's own timestamp. The audio is copied from the reference, and [mp4-muxer](https://github.com/Vanilagy/mp4-muxer) writes the MP4. Nothing is recorded in real time, so no frames are dropped. ### Requirements | | Needed for | |---|---| | **Node.js 22+** | Running the local server (`npm start`). No dependencies to install. | | **Chrome or Edge** | MP4 export (WebCodecs + `requestVideoFrameCallback`). Playback works in any modern browser. | | **FFmpeg / ffprobe** (optional) | Importing your own references, planning sections, rebuilding the showcase, and extracting audio for imported references. | | **Python 3** (optional) | `scripts/import-motionclone.py`. | ## Bring your own references With Python, FFmpeg and ffprobe installed: ```sh python scripts/import-motionclone.py --source /path/to/MotionClone node scripts/plan-sections.mjs # sections + scene cuts + contact sheets ``` Imported media stays local in `.local-media/` and `public/references/` (both ignored by Git) and takes precedence over the showcase. Describe each section's beats in `public/references/drafts.json`. Undescribed sections get placeholder drafts. `npm run showcase` rebuilds `showcase/` from the local library. The importer creates non-destructive segments, extracts thumbnails, and hard-links the source videos when they are on the same drive as this repo (otherwise it copies them). Original files are only read. The server streams byte ranges, so seeking never reads a whole video into memory. ## FAQ and troubleshooting **How do I move through the film frame by frame?** Pause the film, then press `,` to step back one frame or `.` to step forward (1/30 second). Use `Home` to jump to the start and `End` to jump to the end. The left and right arrow keys still jump between sections. **The Download button says "Needs Chrome or Edge".** Export uses WebCodecs and `requestVideoFrameCallback`. Use a current Chrome or Edge. Firefox and Safari can play the preview but can't export. **How long does an export take?** The film is rendered at half speed so no frame is skipped, so expect it to take at least twice the film's length (a minute or more for the 30-second Infinite ad). Keep the tab in front while it renders, because browsers slow down video in background tabs. **My export has no sound.** The showcase ships its audio. For your own imported references the server extracts the audio with FFmpeg on first export, so FFmpeg must be on your `PATH`. **The import failed with "Invalid cross-device link" (EXDEV).** Older versions only hard-linked videos, which only works on one drive. Pull the latest `main`: the importer now copies the video when a link isn't possible. A copy uses extra disk space, so keep MotionClone on the same drive as this repo if space is tight. **"No data/ folder in …" when importing.** `--source` must point at the MotionClone project folder (the one that contains `data/`), not at a single video. **Port 4343 is already in use, or I want to open it from another device.** Set `PORT` and/or `HOST`, for example `PORT=5000 npm start` or `HOST=0.0.0.0 npm start` (default `127.0.0.1:4343`). **The template gallery or editor says "generation not connected".** That's intentional. Generation, rendering services, and Premiere are not connected in this repo, and the server answers those calls with `501 NOT_CONNECTED`. The drafts are authored, not AI-generated. **Can I make vertical clips, cut pauses, or add captions with this?** No. Those are features of Null Studio at [nullmotion.com](https://www.nullmotion.com/), a separate hosted product. Stuck on something else? Ask in the **[Discord](https://discord.gg/zEB4VjmfSb)** or [open an issue](https://github.com/blixvip/NullMotion/issues/new/choose). ## Project layout ``` public/demo.html · demo.mjs · demo.css the preview page and exporter public/drafts.mjs HyperFrames draft engine (beat kinds) public/scraps.mjs hand-built drafts for the Interface reference public/editor.* the earlier launch editor, at /editor showcase/ the three published references scripts/ import, sections, showcase, waveforms, checks server.js · media.js static server, media streaming, audio extraction test/ server, media and editor tests ``` ```sh npm run dev # restart on change npm run check # UI file checks npm test # node --test ``` ## Notes - The browser only calls this project's own origin. - The earlier launch editor (reference timeline, trimming, brand overlay) is at `/editor`, and the original Null Motion template gallery is at `/index.html`. - Bundled GSAP and mp4-muxer keep their licenses; see [THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md](THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md). # Awesome Jev [![Awesome](https://awesome.re/badge.svg)](https://awesome.re)

[Jev](https://docs.typesafe.ai) is TypeSafe's System One model for probability-based yes/no judgments, choices, and scores rather than generated text.

Check permissions and data handling before running a project. Source review is not a runtime test or a security audit.

## Contents

- [Getting Started](#getting-started)
- [Demos](#demos)
- [SDKs and Skills](#sdks-and-skills)
- [Browser and Desktop Tools](#browser-and-desktop-tools)
- [Agent Tools](#agent-tools)
- [Apps and Integrations](#apps-and-integrations)
- [Games and Creative Projects](#games-and-creative-projects)
- [Independent Models](#independent-models)
- [Reading and Research](#reading-and-research)
- [Supporting Drivers](#supporting-drivers)

## Getting Started

Start with the [quick-start example](docs/DIRECTORY.md#20-second-quick-start), then build a [typed classifier](docs/START_HERE.md#build-your-first-typed-classifier), use Jev in an [agent](docs/START_HERE.md#use-jev-in-an-agent), or explore a [local alternative](docs/START_HERE.md#explore-a-local-alternative). The [source notes](docs/REVIEWED.md) record setup, privacy, and evidence limits for the selections below.

## Demos

A few examples to watch before digging into the code. These are creator recordings and publisher previews, not independent benchmarks. Linked previews open the original recording or post.

- [Jev Ultrafast](https://github.com/browser-use/jev-ultrafast/blob/main/README.md) - A flight-search recording where Jev chooses browser actions and elements; a separate model writes field text. Browser Use · @gregpr07.

[![Animated flight-search recording from Browser Use; open the creator post](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/browser-use/jev-ultrafast/1231850a0bf1a0c0341fe408ef1668dbbfdfac46/docs/demo.gif)](https://x.com/gregpr07/status/2100411066966749359)

[![Still preview of the voice-controlled browser; open the creator video on X](https://pbs.twimg.com/amplify_video_thumb/2100577954338373633/img/tbH43kHpUotE3hzK.jpg)](https://x.com/moritzkremb/status/2100577979021832365)

<!-- demo:align-video -->

Each entry links the creator post and records its source and access limits.

The [full creator gallery](docs/DIRECTORY.md#watch-jev-in-action) retains the other videos, images, and attribution. Browse the [X index](docs/X_DEMOS.md), [OpenRouter roundup](docs/OPENROUTER_SHOWCASE.md), or [computer-use comparison](docs/CUA.md) for more examples and limitations.

## SDKs and Skills

- [TypeSafe Python SDK](https://github.com/typesafe-ai/typesafe-sdk-python) - Official Python client with a support-ticket routing example.
- [TypeSafe JavaScript SDK](https://github.com/typesafe-ai/typesafe-sdk-js) - Official JavaScript and TypeScript client.
- [TypeSafe Go SDK](https://github.com/kisshan13/typesafe-ai-go) - Community Go client with typed question builders, response helpers, retries, and runnable examples.
- [Official TypeSafe Skill](https://github.com/typesafe-ai/skills) - Request-writing guidance for Noul, Choice, and Score questions.
- [gut](https://github.com/Kungie/gut) - Python decision API with Jev, local, and OpenAI-compatible backends, plus batching, caching, and human-escalation thresholds.
- [Tenbin](https://github.com/simota/tenbin) - MCP server and skill for linting questions, evaluating labeled examples, and choosing thresholds.
- [wellposed](https://github.com/suraj-phanindra/wellposed) - Offline request linter for missing options, broken state references, and question types.
- [jevrs](https://github.com/luizribeiro/jevrs) - Async Rust client with typed answers, derive macros, and native or WASI transports.
- [Jevify](https://github.com/altryne/jevify) - Agent skill for finding places to use Jev and planning comparisons with existing code.
- [Jev Logs](https://github.com/reachjalil/jevlogs) - Scores log entries to decide which need a closer look.
- [Skillbox](https://github.com/kitze/skillbox) - Self-hosted skill library with optional Jev-based recommendations.

## Browser and Desktop Tools

- [Jev Ultrafast](https://github.com/browser-use/jev-ultrafast) - Browser-action and element selection with a separate model for text entry.
- [Jev Voice Browser](https://github.com/moritzkremb/jev-voice-browser) - Voice-controlled Playwright browser that chooses actions from partial speech and page controls.
- [TypeSafe Computer Use](https://github.com/awlevin/typesafe-computer-use) - Mac automation using local OCR and accessibility data, with Jev choosing the next action.
- [Cua Driver + jev-use](https://github.com/trycua/cua) - Python and TypeScript examples where Jev chooses an action, the driver runs it, and code checks the result.
- [Jev Social](https://github.com/socai-io/jev-social) - Bounded social-research loop using Jev choices and socai in the user's Chrome session.
- [Jev Browser Skill](https://github.com/zurfyx/jev-browser-skill) - Small reference for building and executing browser-action choices.
- [Jev Browser](https://github.com/jkudish/jev-browser) - Playwright browser available as an MCP server, CLI, or library.
- [Jev Browser Use](https://github.com/wy-coliney/jev-browser-use) - Skill using an existing Codex browser connection, with Jev choosing clicks and scrolls.
- [Jev Cua](https://github.com/Eronmmer/jev-cua) - Mac automation through Cua Driver, with optional hosted Jev workflow recommendations.
- [jev-bot](https://github.com/stoopid-computers/jev-bot) - Native Mac controls through a JavaScript MCP session, with optional hosted Jev element selection.

## Agent Tools

- [pi-jev-governor](https://github.com/qianyuxiang-369/pi-jev-governor) - Routes planning, model tier, tool permission, and completion decisions for the pi coding agent, with deterministic gates and human or fail-closed fallbacks.
- [softlint](https://github.com/blazejkustra/softlint) - Checks changed diff hunks against plain-English rules and locates findings on added lines.
- [Jev Dreaming](https://github.com/AdnanQuazi/jev-dreaming) - Experimental memory graph where Jev filters text and judges memory relationships while Gemini writes the memories.
- [fast-jev-compaction](https://github.com/tamaratran/fast-jev-compaction) - Experimental history pruning that uses Jev judgments to keep, truncate or drop tool-call pairs.
- [jev-align](https://github.com/sutro-sh/jev-align) - Improves classifier definitions and scoring rubrics using labels and GEPA-proposed edits.
- [Winnow](https://github.com/GhalebDweikat/winnow) - Claude Code context filter that scores tool-output blocks and keeps hidden text locally recallable.
- [Jev-Mem](https://github.com/libingzheren/Jev-Mem) - Research memory system where Jev organizes graph memories and guides retrieval while a separate model writes answers.
- [patdown](https://github.com/tyler-dot-earth/patdown) - Semantic linter that turns Markdown rules into checks and maps flagged evidence to source lines.
- [Oko](https://github.com/bartlomein/oko) - Code-search CLI and MCP server with local candidate retrieval and optional hosted Jev ranking.
- [jgrep](https://github.com/kyu1204/jgrep) - Semantic matching over code chunks, diff hunks, and CSV rows, published on npm as jevgrep.
- [SemDecide](https://github.com/sharziki/semdecide) - Unix CLI for predicates, choices, scores, JSONL filtering, and CI-friendly exit codes.
- [Leanest](https://github.com/baronunread/leanest) - Playwright and Vitest test selector with an optional Jev judge and run-tests fallback on uncertainty.
- [Supercov](https://github.com/supercorp-ai/supercov) - Coverage, security, and code-quality checks where Jev evaluates source files while test coverage stays local.
- [Foreman](https://github.com/thruwire/foreman) - Checks coding-agent progress and decides when intervention may be needed.
- [jev-belay](https://github.com/valentynkit/jev-belay) - Claude Code Stop hook that checks local run evidence before judging an unverified completion claim.
- [jev-claude-statusline](https://github.com/kevnk/jev-claude-statusline) - Claude Code hooks that estimate task progress with Jev and cache it for a status-line display.
- [Jev MCP](https://github.com/jkudish/jev-mcp) - Tools for checking claims against evidence, screening content, and ranking candidates.
- [TypeSafe MCP](https://github.com/itsmostafa/typesafe-mcp) - Go MCP server for making Jev requests from coding agents.
- [jev_search](https://github.com/caio0452/jev_search) - Experimental file search that ranks candidates by keyword and checks passages with Jev.

✨ AI Game Developer — Godot MCP

[![MCP](https://badge.mcpx.dev 'MCP Server')](https://modelcontextprotocol.io/introduction) [![npm](https://img.shields.io/npm/v/godot-cli?label=godot-cli&logo=npm&labelColor=333A41 'godot-cli on npm')](https://www.npmjs.com/package/godot-cli) [![Godot](https://img.shields.io/badge/Godot-4.3%2B-478CBF?style=flat&logo=godotengine&logoColor=white&labelColor=333A41 'Godot 4.3+, C#/.NET (mono)')](https://godotengine.org/) [![Godot Editor](https://img.shields.io/badge/Editor-X?style=flat&logo=godotengine&logoColor=white&labelColor=333A41&color=2A2A2A 'Godot Editor supported')](https://godotengine.org/) [![Godot Runtime](https://img.shields.io/badge/Runtime-X?style=flat&logo=godotengine&logoColor=white&labelColor=333A41&color=2A2A2A 'Godot Runtime supported')](https://godotengine.org/) [![.NET](https://img.shields.io/badge/.NET-8.0-512BD4?style=flat&labelColor=333A41 '.NET 8')](https://dotnet.microsoft.com/) [![release](https://github.com/IvanMurzak/Godot-MCP/workflows/release/badge.svg 'release')](https://github.com/IvanMurzak/Godot-MCP/actions/workflows/release.yml)
[![Discord](https://img.shields.io/badge/Discord-Join-7289da?logo=discord&logoColor=white&labelColor=333A41 'Join')](https://discord.gg/cfbdMZX99G) [![Stars](https://img.shields.io/github/stars/IvanMurzak/Godot-MCP 'Stars')](https://github.com/IvanMurzak/Godot-MCP/stargazers) [![Docker Image](https://img.shields.io/badge/Docker-Image-2496ED?style=flat&logo=docker&logoColor=white&labelColor=333A41 'Docker Image')](https://hub.docker.com/r/aigamedeveloper/mcp-server) [![License](https://img.shields.io/github/license/IvanMurzak/Godot-MCP?label=License&labelColor=333A41)](https://github.com/IvanMurzak/Godot-MCP/blob/main/LICENSE) [![Stand With Ukraine](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/vshymanskyy/StandWithUkraine/main/badges/StandWithUkraine.svg)](https://stand-with-ukraine.pp.ua)

                                

`Godot MCP` is an AI-powered game development assistant **for the Godot Editor**. Connect **Claude**, **Cursor**, **Copilot**, or any MCP-aware agent to Godot and let it inspect and drive your project — create nodes, edit scenes, manage resources and scripts, capture screenshots, and more. Godot-MCP is the Godot counterpart of [Unity-MCP](https://github.com/IvanMurzak/Unity-MCP): a C# **editor addon** that exposes Godot Editor operations as **AI Tools** and connects them to an MCP server through the same hosted cloud backend ([ai-game.dev](https://ai-game.dev)) that powers Unity-MCP — or your own self-hosted server. The MCP / reflection stack is **not forked**: it is shared with Unity-MCP and consumed from [nuget.org](https://www.nuget.org/) as `PackageReference`s. > **[💬 Join our Discord Server](https://discord.gg/cfbdMZX99G)** — Ask questions, showcase your work, and connect with other developers! ## ![Features](https://github.com/IvanMurzak/Godot-MCP/blob/main/docs/img/promo/hazzard-features.svg?raw=true) - ✔️ **AI agents** — Use the best agents from **Anthropic**, **OpenAI**, **Google**, or any other provider with no vendor lock-in - ✔️ **24 built-in Tools** — [MCP Tools](#tools-reference) across 9 families for operating the Godot Editor, led by [RQL](docs/rql.md): one query language for the whole editor - ✔️ **C# & GDScript** — Read, create, and update both `.cs` and `.gd` scripts, and attach them to nodes - ✔️ **Scene & Node control** — Query and edit the scene tree, Godot properties (GDScript variables included), `.tscn` scenes and `.tres`/`.res` resources with RQL — bulk, all-or-nothing, undoable - ✔️ **Visual feedback** — Capture viewport, camera, and isolated-node screenshots the LLM can inspect - ✔️ **Call anything** — `call CallMethod("name", [args])` reaches any Godot method (GDScript ones too); in a running game, find and call C# methods via [ReflectorNet](https://www.nuget.org/packages/com.IvanMurzak.ReflectorNet) - ✔️ **Cloud or self-hosted** — Connect to `ai-game.dev` out of the box, or point at your own server - ✔️ **Natural conversation** — Chat with AI like you would with a human ![AI Game Developer — Godot MCP](https://github.com/IvanMurzak/Godot-MCP/blob/main/docs/img/promo/hazzard-divider.svg?raw=true) # Quick Start Get up and running from a terminal using the [`godot-cli`](https://www.npmjs.com/package/godot-cli) (the Godot analog of `unity-mcp-cli`) — no manual file copying or csproj editing required: ```bash # 1. Install godot-cli npm install -g godot-cli # 2. (Optional) Scaffold a fresh Godot C# project — skip if you already have one godot-cli create-project --dotnet ./MyGodotProject # 3. Install the godot_mcp addon: downloads addons/godot_mcp/ from the matching # GitHub release, adds the required NuGet packages + the extension-catalog # EmbeddedResource to your .csproj, and enables the plugin in project.godot — # all idempotently godot-cli install-plugin ./MyGodotProject # 4. Sign in to the ai-game.dev cloud — OAuth 2.1 device login (opens a browser, # saves a machine-wide credential the editor plugin auto-adopts; no token to copy) godot-cli login # 5. Pick an AI agent (Claude Code, Cursor, Copilot, …) and write its MCP config — # pinned to THIS project's cloud route by default (pass --no-pin for the bare URL) godot-cli setup-mcp claude-code ./MyGodotProject # 6. Open the Godot editor — builds the C# assembly first (so the addon loads on # the very first open) then auto-connects with the right GODOT_MCP_* env vars godot-cli open ./MyGodotProject # 7. Wait until the plugin answers the readiness probe godot-cli wait-for-ready ./MyGodotProject ``` That's it. Ask your AI *"Create 3 cubes in a circle with radius 2"* and watch it happen. ✨ > **Offline / dev install:** `install-plugin --source /addons/godot_mcp` copies the addon from > a local directory instead of downloading it. Prefer the matching release version with > `install-plugin --version ` if you need a specific addon build. The manual route (copy the > addon + add the NuGet packages yourself) is still documented under [Installation](#installation) > Steps 1–2 for the Asset Library / hand-managed flows. > See the [full CLI documentation](https://github.com/IvanMurzak/Godot-MCP/blob/main/cli/README.md) for every command, editor-resolution order, and connection env vars. # Contents - [Quick Start](#quick-start) - [Tools Reference](#tools-reference) - [Requirements](#requirements) - [Installation](#installation) - [Step 1: Add the addon](#step-1-add-the-addon) - [Option A — Godot Asset Library (recommended)](#option-a--godot-asset-library-recommended) - [Option B — GitHub Release zip](#option-b--github-release-zip) - [Option C — copy from source](#option-c--copy-from-source) - [Step 2: Add the NuGet packages](#step-2-add-the-nuget-packages) - [Step 3: Install an AI agent](#step-3-install-an-ai-agent) - [Connect](#connect) - [Cloud mode (default) — ai-game.dev](#cloud-mode-default--ai-gamedev) - [Custom mode — your own server](#custom-mode--your-own-server) - [Godot `MCP Server` setup](#godot-mcp-server-setup) - [Local server — let the addon download & run it for you](#local-server--let-the-addon-download--run-it-for-you) - [Build & run the server manually (advanced)](#build--run-the-server-manually-advanced) - [Customize Tools](#customize-tools) - [Runtime usage (in-game)](#runtime-usage-in-game) - [Capturing in-game runtime errors](#capturing-in-game-runtime-errors) - [Sample: a live game-state tool](#sample-a-live-game-state-tool) - [Where the server URL and token come from](#where-the-server-url-and-token-come-from) - [Security: opt-in only, default OFF](#security-opt-in-only-default-off) - [How Godot MCP Architecture Works](#how-godot-mcp-architecture-works) - [Building & contributing](#building--contributing) - [License](#license) ![AI Game Developer — Godot MCP](https://github.com/IvanMurzak/Godot-MCP/blob/main/docs/img/promo/hazzard-divider.svg?raw=true) # Tools Reference Godot-MCP ships **24 built-in tools** grouped into **9 families**. The editor's data layer is [RQL](docs/rql.md) (Reflection Query Language): `rql-query`, `rql-mutate` and `rql-schema` read and change scene nodes, Godot properties, resources, files, scenes and editor state in one query instead of one tool per operation (they replace the former `node-*`, `scene-*`, `resource-*`, `filesystem-*` and `editor-*` tools; in the editor also `console-*` and `reflection-*`, which stay available in a running game). With the default `toolFormat` (`Rql`) the other tools take RQL values as arguments and return compact text; `Json` keeps ReflectorNet's JSON schemas and results. Screenshots return a PNG image. All editor tools are available immediately after the addon is enabled — no extra configuration required. The **runtime-errors**, **console** and **reflection** families serve the *running game* (the in-game runtime, see [Runtime usage](#runtime-usage-in-game)); runtime-errors is **OFF by default** — opt in with `builder.WithRuntimeErrorCapture()` (see [Capturing in-game runtime errors](#capturing-in-game-runtime-errors)). | Family | Tools | What it does | | --- | --- | --- | | **ping** | `ping` | Lightweight readiness probe — echoes a message back, or returns `pong`. Verifies the end-to-end
